docs.title: vexy-mkdocs-tools
docs.text:
vexy-mkdocs-tools is a command-line tool that builds a documentation site from a folder of Markdown files. It installs ProperDocs, the MaterialX theme and a fixed set of MkDocs plugins, and runs the same build steps that every FontLab and Vexy documentation site uses.

uvx vexy-mkdocs-tools build

The tool has two command names, vexy-mkdocs-tools and vmt. They run the same program.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
A site repository that uses this tool contains only Markdown and one configuration file:

my-site/
├── mkdocs/mkdocs.yml     # site configuration
├── src_docs/md/          # Markdown source
└── docs/                 # generated site, served by GitHub Pages

vmt build turns src_docs/md/ into a static site in docs/ in four steps:

  1. Format. If flowmark is on your PATH, it reformats the Markdown in src_docs/md/ in place. If not, it prints a warning and continues.
  2. Clean. It deletes everything in docs/ except a file named CNAME.
  3. Build. It runs properdocs build with mkdocs/mkdocs.yml as the configuration and docs/ as the output folder.
  4. Mark. It creates an empty docs/.nojekyll file, so GitHub Pages serves the files as they are instead of running Jekyll on them.

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text: Without this tool, each site repository has to list the same Python packages and carry its own copy of the build script. With it, the package list and the script live in one place, and a site repository only needs its Markdown and its mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: What it installs
docs.text:
Installing vexy-mkdocs-tools also installs:

Package Minimum version Purpose properdocs 1.6.7 The site generator; its configuration format is MkDocs' mkdocs.yml mkdocs-materialx 10.1.4 The materialx theme and its materialx/* plugins pymdown-extensions 10.2 Markdown extensions mkdocs-awesome-nav 3.3 Plugin awesome-nav: customize the navigation structure mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin 7.2 Plugin include-markdown: include one Markdown file in another mkdocs-llmstxt 0.2 Plugin llmstxt: generate an /llms.txt file mkdocs-copy-to-llm 0.2 Plugin copy-to-llm: add "Copy to LLM" buttons mkdocs-rss-plugin 1.17 Plugin rss: generate RSS and JSON feeds fire 0.7 The command-line interface loguru 0.7 Logging

The optional flowmark extra adds flowmark 0.6.5 or later for the format step.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text:
vmt [GLOBAL FLAGS] COMMAND [COMMAND FLAGS]

vexy-mkdocs-tools and vmt are the same program. python -m vexy_mkdocs_tools also runs it. The command line is built with Python Fire, so --help after any command shows its flags:

vmt --help
vmt build --help

docs.title: Global flags
docs.text:
These flags choose the folders the commands work on. Relative paths are resolved against the current working directory.

Flag Short Default Meaning --root -r Found by searching upwards The site root folder --config -c <root>/mkdocs/mkdocs.yml The ProperDocs configuration file --docs -d <root>/docs The output folder --src -s <root>/src_docs/md The Markdown folder that Flowmark formats

Fire accepts these flags before or after the command name, so vmt --root site build and vmt build --root site do the same thing.

--src only tells the format step where the Markdown is. ProperDocs reads its source folder from docs_dir in the configuration file. See Site configuration.

Without --root, the tool searches for the site root before it runs any command. See Site layout.

docs.title: build
docs.text:
Runs the full pipeline.

vmt build [--verbose] [--no-format]
Flag Short Default Meaning --verbose -v off Log at DEBUG level --no-format (also --no_format) -n off Skip the Flowmark step

Steps, in order:

  1. Unless --no-format is given, run Flowmark over the --src folder (see format). If the folder does not exist, the build stops with source Markdown directory missing: <path>.
  2. Delete everything in the --docs folder except CNAME. Create the folder if it does not exist.
  3. Stop with mkdocs config missing: <path> if the configuration file does not exist.
  4. Run properdocs build -f <config> -d <docs> from the site root.
  5. Create <docs>/.nojekyll.

If any step fails, the tool logs the error and exits with status 1. A failed ProperDocs run is reported as build failed (exit <code>).

docs.title: serve
docs.text:
Starts the ProperDocs development server with live reload.

vmt serve [--verbose]

The tool runs properdocs serve -f <config> from the site root. ProperDocs builds the preview into a temporary folder, so docs/ is left alone. Stop the server with Ctrl+C; the tool prints Server stopped.

docs.title: clean
docs.text:
Empties the output folder without building.

vmt clean [--verbose]

Deletes every file and folder in --docs except CNAME, and logs Cleaned <docs> (preserved CNAME). Symbolic links are removed, not followed.

docs.title: format
docs.text:
Formats the Markdown source in place with Flowmark.

vmt format [--verbose]

The tool runs this command from the site root:

flowmark --inplace --nobackup --semantic --cleanups --smartquotes --ellipses --width 0 <src>

With these options Flowmark rewrites the files without keeping backups, applies its cleanups, turns straight quotes into typographic quotes and ... into …, and does not wrap lines.

If flowmark is not on the PATH, the command logs this warning and returns without an error:

flowmark not on PATH; install the [flowmark] extra (`uv pip install vexy-mkdocs-tools[flowmark]`) to enable this step

docs.title: version
docs.text:
Prints the installed package version, for example 0.1.1.

vmt version

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Messages go to standard error in the form LEVEL | message. The default level is INFO. Two settings change it:

  • --verbose on any command except version sets the level to DEBUG. At that level clean and build also log every file they remove.
  • The VMT_LOG_LEVEL environment variable sets the level when --verbose is not given, for example VMT_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING vmt build.

ProperDocs prints its own messages in its own format (INFO - …). The two settings above do not affect them.

docs.title: Site configuration
docs.text: vmt does not have a configuration file of its own. It passes mkdocs/mkdocs.yml to ProperDocs, which reads it with the same keys as MkDocs. This page covers the settings that matter when the file lives in mkdocs/ and the bundled packages are used.

docs.title: A minimal configuration
docs.text:
site_name: My site
docs_dir: ../src_docs/md
theme:
  name: materialx

docs.title: docs_dir
docs.text:
ProperDocs resolves a relative docs_dir against the folder that contains the configuration file. The file is in mkdocs/, so the Markdown folder is ../src_docs/md. Without this line, ProperDocs looks for mkdocs/docs/.

vmt does not pass the source folder to ProperDocs. The --src flag only affects the Flowmark step.

docs.title: site_dir
docs.text: You do not need to set site_dir. vmt build passes -d <docs> to properdocs build, which overrides it.

docs.title: theme
docs.text:
The bundled theme package, mkdocs-materialx, registers the theme name materialx, and that is the only theme ProperDocs accepts with the bundled packages. Other names fail:

ERROR   -  Config value 'theme': Unrecognised theme name: 'material'. The available installed themes are: materialx

ProperDocs does not ship the classic mkdocs and readthedocs themes. Asking for one prints a hint such as pip install properdocs-theme-mkdocs.

docs.title: Plugins you can enable
docs.text:
These plugin names are available after installing vexy-mkdocs-tools:

Plugin name Package search properdocs materialx/blog, materialx/group, materialx/info, materialx/meta, materialx/offline, materialx/optimize, materialx/privacy, materialx/search, materialx/social, materialx/tags mkdocs-materialx awesome-nav mkdocs-awesome-nav include-markdown mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin llmstxt mkdocs-llmstxt copy-to-llm mkdocs-copy-to-llm rss mkdocs-rss-plugin document-dates mkdocs-document-dates, installed as a dependency of mkdocs-materialx

List them in the usual way:

plugins:
  - search
  - awesome-nav
  - include-markdown

Each plugin has its own options; see the documentation of its package.

docs.title: Markdown extensions
docs.text:
pymdown-extensions is installed, so you can enable any pymdownx.* extension:

markdown_extensions:
  - admonition
  - toc:
      permalink: true
  - pymdownx.highlight
  - pymdownx.superfences
  - pymdownx.tabbed:
      alternate_style: true

docs.title: A fuller example
docs.text:
site_name: My site
site_url: https://example.com/
docs_dir: ../src_docs/md
theme:
  name: materialx
  features:
    - navigation.sections
    - content.code.copy
plugins:
  - search
  - include-markdown
markdown_extensions:
  - admonition
  - pymdownx.superfences
nav:
  - Home: index.md

Note

Some plugins need options before they run. For example, llmstxt without a sections option stops the build with Plugin 'llmstxt' option 'sections': Required configuration not provided. Check each plugin's documentation; vmt passes the file to ProperDocs unchanged.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: vexy-mkdocs-tools is the shared build tool for many documentation sites. A change to what vmt build produces changes every one of those sites. Add a test that proves the new output is correct before you change the pipeline.

docs.title: Set up a development environment
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-mkdocs-tools.git
cd vexy-mkdocs-tools

  2. Install the package and the development tools (pytest, pytest-cov, ruff):

    uv sync --extra dev

docs.title: Run the checks
docs.text:
uv run python -m pytest -q
uvx ruff check src tests

tests/test_cli.py covers:

  • _clean_docs: creates a missing folder, and keeps CNAME while deleting everything else.
  • _find_repo_root: finds the root from a nested folder, and raises BuildError when there is none.
  • End-to-end builds of a small fixture site, which check that the page is rendered, .nojekyll is written and src_docs/md/CNAME reaches the output. These tests are skipped when properdocs is not on the PATH.

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs ruff, the tests and a package build on Python 3.12 and 3.13 for every push and pull request to main.

docs.title: Code layout
docs.text:
File Contents src/vexy_mkdocs_tools/cli.py The whole tool: the CLI class with build, serve, clean, format and version, plus helper functions src/vexy_mkdocs_tools/__init__.py Exposes __version__ src/vexy_mkdocs_tools/__main__.py Lets python -m vexy_mkdocs_tools run the tool src/vexy_mkdocs_tools/__version__.py Written by hatch-vcs at build time; ignored by git

Every source file starts with a this_file: comment that gives its path.

docs.title: Build the package and this documentation
docs.text:
./build.sh            # documentation and package
./build.sh docs       # documentation only
./build.sh package    # dist/*.whl and dist/*.tar.gz, then twine check

This documentation does not use vmt. Its source is in src_docs/md/, its configuration in src_docs/mkdocs.yml, and src_docs/build.sh builds it into docs/ with ProperDocs and MaterialX in strict mode. For a live preview:

src_docs/build.sh serve

The Docs workflow rebuilds docs/ and commits it after every push to main that changes src_docs/.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
The version comes from the latest vX.Y.Z git tag through hatch-vcs.

./publish.sh releases from a local machine:

  1. uvx gitnextver commits pending changes, tags the next vX.Y.Z and pushes.
  2. ./build.sh package builds the wheel and source distribution.
  3. uv publish dist/* uploads them. It needs UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN or another uv publish credential.

The pushed tag also starts .github/workflows/release.yml. It lints, tests and builds again, uploads to PyPI with Trusted Publishing, and creates a GitHub release. The upload uses skip-existing: true, so it does not fail when publish.sh has already uploaded that version.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or later.
  • uv is recommended. Plain pip also works.

docs.title: Run without installing
docs.text:
uvx downloads the package into a cached environment and runs it:

uvx vexy-mkdocs-tools build

To include the optional Flowmark formatter in the same run:

uvx --with flowmark vexy-mkdocs-tools build

docs.title: Install into an environment
docs.text:
uv pip install vexy-mkdocs-tools

With the Flowmark formatter:

uv pip install "vexy-mkdocs-tools[flowmark]"

With pip, use the same package names:

pip install "vexy-mkdocs-tools[flowmark]"

Both commands also install ProperDocs, the MaterialX theme and the bundled plugins, listed on the home page.

docs.title: Install as a tool
docs.text:
To keep vmt on your PATH without activating an environment:

uv tool install vexy-mkdocs-tools

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
vmt looks for a site before it runs any command, including version. Run the check from inside a site folder (see Site layout), or name a folder with --root:

vmt --root path/to/site version

The command prints the installed version, for example 0.1.1.

Note

Outside a site folder and without --root, every command stops with a BuildError: cannot locate site root … traceback. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page creates a new documentation site and builds it with vmt.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• uv installed.
  • An empty folder for the site, here called my-site.

docs.title: Create the site
docs.text:
1. Create the three folders the tool expects:

    mkdir -p my-site/mkdocs my-site/src_docs/md my-site/docs
cd my-site

  2. Create mkdocs/mkdocs.yml with this content:

    site_name: My site
docs_dir: ../src_docs/md
theme:
  name: materialx

    docs_dir is resolved against the folder that holds mkdocs.yml, so ../src_docs/md points from mkdocs/ to the Markdown folder. The theme name is materialx, not material.

  3. Create the first page, src_docs/md/index.md:

    # Hello

This is my site.

  4. Build the site:

    uvx vexy-mkdocs-tools build

The tool prints its steps:

WARNING  | flowmark not on PATH; install the [flowmark] extra (`uv pip install vexy-mkdocs-tools[flowmark]`) to enable this step
INFO     | Cleaned /…/my-site/docs (preserved CNAME)
INFO     | Running: properdocs build -f /…/my-site/mkdocs/mkdocs.yml -d /…/my-site/docs
INFO     | Build complete

docs/ now holds the site: index.html, 404.html, assets/, search/, sitemap.xml, sitemap.xml.gz and an empty .nojekyll.

The warning only means that the format step was skipped. To run it, use uvx --with flowmark vexy-mkdocs-tools build. To skip it without a warning, add --no-format.

docs.title: Preview while you write
docs.text:
uvx vexy-mkdocs-tools serve

This runs properdocs serve with the same configuration. Press Ctrl+C to stop it; the tool then prints Server stopped.

docs.title: Add a custom domain
docs.text:
1. Put the domain in src_docs/md/CNAME:

    echo docs.example.com > src_docs/md/CNAME

  2. Build again.

ProperDocs copies every file that is not Markdown from src_docs/md/ to docs/, so docs/CNAME is written on every build. A CNAME that exists only in docs/ does not survive a full build; see Site layout.

docs.title: Publish with GitHub Pages
docs.text:
1. Commit mkdocs/, src_docs/ and the built docs/ folder.
  2. In the repository settings on GitHub, set Pages to deploy from the default branch and the /docs folder.

The .nojekyll file that vmt build writes tells GitHub Pages to publish the files without running Jekyll.

docs.title: Site layout
docs.text: vmt expects every site to use the same folder structure. This page describes that structure and how the tool finds it.

docs.title: The default layout
docs.text:
<root>/
├── mkdocs/
│   └── mkdocs.yml      # --config
├── src_docs/
│   └── md/             # --src: Markdown source
│       ├── index.md
│       └── CNAME       # optional custom domain
└── docs/               # --docs: build output
Path Role Flag to change it mkdocs/mkdocs.yml ProperDocs configuration --config src_docs/md/ Markdown source; Flowmark formats this folder --src docs/ Generated site; GitHub Pages serves it --docs

docs.title: How the site root is found
docs.text:
When you do not pass --root, the tool starts in the current working directory and checks it and then each parent folder in turn. The first folder that contains both of these is the site root:

  • a file mkdocs/mkdocs.yml, and
  • a folder src_docs/.

So you can run vmt build from the site root or from any folder below it, such as src_docs/md/chapter-1/.

If no folder matches, the tool stops with:

BuildError: cannot locate site root (no mkdocs/mkdocs.yml + src_docs/ found walking up from cwd). Pass --root explicitly.

The search runs before the command itself, so it applies to every command, including version and clean. With --root, the search is skipped and the named folder is used as it is; the tool does not check that it has the expected contents.

docs.title: The output folder
docs.text:
vmt build and vmt clean delete everything in docs/ except CNAME. Do not keep hand-written files in docs/. Put files that should appear in the built site, such as images, downloads or CNAME, in src_docs/md/. ProperDocs copies every file that is not Markdown from there into docs/, keeping its relative path.

After a build, docs/ always contains an empty .nojekyll file.

docs.title: The CNAME file
docs.text:
GitHub Pages reads the custom domain from docs/CNAME. Keep the file in src_docs/md/CNAME.

vmt clean keeps an existing docs/CNAME. A full vmt build does not: after the tool's own clean step, properdocs build empties the output folder again before it writes the site. A CNAME that exists only in docs/ is therefore gone after vmt build. A CNAME in src_docs/md/ is copied back on every build.

docs.title: Using a different layout
docs.text:
Pass the paths explicitly. For example, for a site that keeps its configuration at the top level and its Markdown in content/:

vmt --root . --config mkdocs.yml --src content --docs public build

Remember to set docs_dir: content in that configuration file as well, because --src does not change where ProperDocs reads from.

docs.title: Cannot locate site root
docs.text:
Any command, including vmt version, stops with a traceback that ends in:

vexy_mkdocs_tools.cli.BuildError: cannot locate site root (no mkdocs/mkdocs.yml + src_docs/ found walking up from cwd). Pass --root explicitly.

The tool searched the current folder and all its parents and found none that holds both mkdocs/mkdocs.yml and src_docs/. Do one of these:

  • Change into the site folder, or any folder below it, and run the command again.
  • Pass the site folder: vmt --root path/to/site build.
  • If the site uses another layout, pass every path. See Site layout.

docs.title: mkdocs config missing: <path>
docs.text: build or serve found no file at the --config path. The default is <root>/mkdocs/mkdocs.yml. Check the file name and the --root you passed.

docs.title: docs_dir is not an existing directory
docs.text:
ProperDocs stops with a message like:

ERROR   -  Config value 'docs_dir': The path '/…/my-site/mkdocs/docs' isn't an existing directory.
Aborted with a configuration error!
ERROR    | build failed (exit 1)

The configuration file has no docs_dir, or a wrong one. ProperDocs resolves it against the folder of mkdocs.yml, so add:

docs_dir: ../src_docs/md

docs.title: Unrecognised theme name: 'material'
docs.text:
ProperDocs prints:

ERROR   -  Config value 'theme': Unrecognised theme name: 'material'. The available installed themes are: materialx

The bundled theme is called materialx. Change the theme block to:

theme:
  name: materialx

docs.title: flowmark not on PATH
docs.text:
The format step was skipped because the flowmark command is not installed in the environment. The build continues. Either install it:

uv pip install "vexy-mkdocs-tools[flowmark]"
# or, for a one-off run
uvx --with flowmark vexy-mkdocs-tools build

or skip the step with vmt build --no-format.

docs.title: source Markdown directory missing: <path>
docs.text: The format step runs before anything else and needs the --src folder, by default <root>/src_docs/md. Create it, pass the right path with --src, or skip formatting with --no-format.

docs.title: build failed (exit <code>)
docs.text: properdocs build returned an error. Its own messages appear above this line, in the ERROR - … format. Fix the reported problem in mkdocs.yml or the Markdown. A common case is a plugin that needs options, such as llmstxt without sections.

docs.title: The custom domain disappears after a build
docs.text: The CNAME file was only in docs/. A full build empties docs/ twice: once in the tool's own clean step, which keeps CNAME, and once inside properdocs build, which does not. Move the file to src_docs/md/CNAME.

docs.title: Files I added to docs/ are gone
docs.text: vmt build and vmt clean delete everything in docs/ except CNAME. Keep extra files in src_docs/md/; ProperDocs copies them into docs/ on each build.

docs.title: Too much or too little output
docs.text:
• Add --verbose to see DEBUG messages, including every file that clean removes.
  • Set VMT_LOG_LEVEL=WARNING to hide the tool's INFO messages.
